requirements.summary: The complete prepared tree contained two directories and two files. Both files retained their baseline SHA-256 hashes after the repair and again after restart, while the final tree still contained all four entries.

requirements.requirement: Make the existing data owned by inventorysvc and readable by inventory-readers.
requirements.summary: The required account and group exist. Every observed directory is owned by inventorysvc:inventory-readers with mode 2750, and every observed file has the same ownership with mode 0640. These modes provide the reader group traversal and read access; owner reads also succeeded before and after restart.

requirements.requirement: Make /srv/inventory inaccessible to users outside the owner and reader group.
requirements.summary: All observed entries have zero permission bits for others. Direct tests as the unrelated nobody account could neither list the directory nor read a file, both before and after restart.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied. The provider-wide restart protocol is also well supported: a healthy task state and boot identity were captured before restart, restart was acknowledged, the node was temporarily unreachable, a different boot identity appeared, and identities, metadata, hashes, owner access, and denial of unauthorized access were recovered. Fixed lifecycle boot observations independently corroborate the transition. The only notable deficiency is retained temporary evidence residue.
limitations: Reader-group access was established directly through group ownership and permission bits, but no separate non-owner account belonging to inventory-readers was used for a behavioral read test.

Systemd failed-service collection is unsupported on this Alpine/OpenRC node, so broad service-health evidence is limited; node reachability, SSH listening state, task data, identities, and permissions did recover.
Lifecycle snapshots inventory only bounded system state and do not independently enumerate /srv/inventory; task-specific commands provide the direct final-state evidence.
Requirement preserve-existing-contents cited unknown evidence IDs: prepared-inventory-data

operational_hygiene.summary: The account creation, ownership/mode repair, verification, and mandatory restart were causally connected to the requested outcome or evidence protocol. No new listener, damaged package state, or unrelated system mutation is shown. However, three evidence-related commands left nine unnecessary temporary artifacts: four nobody-test output/error files from cmd-03b58ad79ead48f5, /tmp/benchmark-reboot.log from cmd-a226c02f14a74594, and four post-restart test files from cmd-1178af782b6a45af. All remained at the final snapshot rather than being cleaned up; they are bounded, low-risk residue.
